content:
The headline is one thing, but the interest survey results for a forthcoming iPhone Ultra tell a very different story

However, Apple shouldn't get too excited about that, because the willingness to pay is far below the expected retail price……

The survey, reported by CNET, began by stating the 75% figure.

A lack of broad interest is unsurprising: the real story is that a full quarter of US adults find the concept appealing.

Most Liked Comment from Throwback

I'm interested, but not at $2,000. I'll check it out in an Apple Store first.

Unsurprisingly, interest varied sharply by generation:

  • Baby Boomers: 13%
  • Gen X: 23%
  • Gen Z: 31%
  • Millennials: 32%

If the actual purchase rate for Apple's first-generation foldable iPhone ends up being anything more than the low single digits, I'll be very surprised, and my view seems supported by the survey's data on willingness to pay.

Gen Z was willing to pay the most, at $919, while the overall US adult average was $781. The actual price is highly unlikely to come in below $2,000.

As production costs come down, future generations of Apple's foldable will likely get somewhat cheaper, but they will never approach the prices respondents said they were willing to pay. Though Apple is famously good at getting consumers to part with far more money than they initially claim to be willing to spend when the company rolls out shiny new products, my own expectation is that, due to both the price and the lack of true portability, this product will forever remain a relatively niche offering.
